key_insight: Factorial analysis identified HVOF settings associated with acceptable hardness, porosity, and oxide content in Cr₃C₂-20(Ni20Cr) coatings on Ti6Al4V.
engineering_relevance: The reported settings—150 mm standoff, 25 g/min powder feed, 475 NLPM hydrogen, and 205 NLPM oxygen—provide a starting point for process qualification.
method: Use a full factorial design with 24 experimental runs and two levels per input factor.
Apply ANOVA to quantify spray-parameter contributions to coating properties.
Use Pareto charts to examine parameter interaction effects.
evidence_signal: Coating responses were measured for each experimental run, but the abstract gives no numerical property results or uncertainty estimates.
watch_item: Validate the reported settings for the intended equipment and service conditions before treating them as transferable process specifications.
paper_title: Investigation of the Effect of HVOF Spray Parameters on the Quality Properties of Cr3C2-20(Ni20Cr) Coating on Ti6Al4V Substrate
